items.q: Why does THC affect time, memory, appetite, pain, and mood so broadly?
items.a: **CB1** is among the brain's most widely expressed GPCRs. THC is a **high-affinity partial agonist** that outcompetes endogenous **anandamide/2-AG** tone without matching 2-AG's efficacy — wide receptor occupancy explains wide subjective effects.

items.q: Does raising natural anandamide get you high?
items.a: No. **FAAH inhibitors** elevate anandamide without psychoactivity — "no one can guess." Intoxication requires **exogenous THC** at superphysiological receptor occupancy; you don't need much THC in the brain to produce a high.

sections.title: THC, CBD, and the indica/sativa myth

items.q: Is CBD a simple antidote that buffers THC?
items.a: Mechanisms are **dose- and context-dependent**. At clinical doses CBD can inhibit hepatic CYPs and **potentiate THC** (Ryan Vandrey blinded studies) rather than buffer it. Pediatric epilepsy benefits may partly come from slowing other anti-epileptic drug metabolism.

items.q: Do indica and sativa labels predict how you'll feel?
items.a: **No consistent biological basis** — strain names are largely **marketing folklore**. Terpene/cannabinoid profiles vary batch-to-batch; **expectation and set/setting** dominate "couch-lock" vs "energy" stories.

items.q: Why are edibles riskier than smoking for overdose?
items.a: Inhaled cannabis hits blood THC fast, enabling **self-titration** (~**100 ng/mL** peaks in experienced users). **Edibles** delay onset **30–90+ minutes**, so people stack doses — ER visits disproportionately come from **oral overdose**, not smoking.

items.q: What's the problem with dabs and distillate carts?
items.a: Plants biologically top out around **25–30% THC**; concentrates push **60–90%+** and **break self-titration**. Users can't reliably down-regulate intake, correlating with tolerance, dependence symptoms, and acute adverse events.

Acute THC psychotic episodes are **real but uncommon**. The link between **early heavy / high-potency use** and earlier schizophrenia onset is a **robust association**, but **causality isn't provable** (shared genetics, prodromal self-medication). Vulnerable people can get worse positive symptoms.

items.q: How common is cannabis use disorder?
items.a: Roughly **9–10% lifetime risk** (~**1 in 11** users), higher with early/heavy use — distinct from casual habit. Withdrawal (irritability, sleep disruption, anxiety, appetite change) is clinically meaningful; tolerance tracks **CB1 downregulation**.

items.q: Did legalization create a teen cannabis epidemic?
items.a: Canada/US data: biggest post-legalization increases in **55+** (especially women) and some young adults; **teen use largely flat** (already ~**35–40%** lifetime by grade 12). Legal ≠ safe — public conflates legality with harmlessness while edible/hyperemesis ER visits rose.

items.q: Is THC a good long-term sleep aid?
items.a: THC can **shorten sleep latency** but **reduces REM**; Hill flags long-term sleep-architecture concerns — not a sustainable sleep solution. Anxiety is **biphasic** (low dose anxiolytic for some, high dose → panic); PTSD fear-extinction data is promising preclinically but human trials remain mixed.
